name: Glimepiride
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Glimepiride is a sulfonylurea whose metabolites (M1, which has some glucose-lowering activity in animals, and M2) are excreted in urine and accumulate as kidney function falls. The US label starts all patients with kidney impairment at 1 mg once daily with slow titration because of hypoglycemia; it gives no CrCl cut-off and no dialysis dosing.
kidney_function_basis: Label PK studies grouped creatinine clearance (CLcr >50, 20–50, <20 mL/min); dose advice is for 'renal impairment' without a number.

bands.recommendation: Start 1 or 2 mg once daily with breakfast; increase by 1 to 2 mg every 1 to 2 weeks; maximum 8 mg/day (label). Older adults: start 1 mg.

Start 1 mg once daily and titrate slowly (label 2.1, 8.6): hypoglycemia risk is higher in kidney impairment, and the M1 and M2 metabolites accumulate (M1 AUC 2.3-fold and M2 AUC 8.6-fold higher at CrCl <20). Studied at CrCl 10–60 mL/min with doses of 1 to 8 mg.

Studied at CrCl 10–60 mL/min with doses of 1 to 8 mg. No separate advice for CrCl <15; hypoglycemia can be prolonged. Specialist judgment.

hd: Not studied in dialysis; the label gives no dialysis dose. Removal by hemodialysis unlikely (over 99.5% protein-bound). Specialist input; prefer agents with lower hypoglycemia risk.
pd: Not studied; no dose in label. Specialist input.
crrt: No data. Specialist input; insulin usually preferred in acute illness.
dialyzable: Not stated; unlikely (protein binding over 99.5%; label).
monitoring: Blood glucose (hypoglycemia, which can be prolonged), hemoglobin A1c, kidney function. Hold in acute illness with poor intake.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not recommended in pediatric patients (adverse effects on weight and hypoglycemia; label 8.4).

renal.recommendation: Not approved for children; kidney dosing not applicable.
